title: Digital Notes and Recall
passage:
People encounter this issue in everyday life, yet common experience can make its causes difficult to notice. A familiar outcome may have several contributing factors, and changing one factor can alter the balance among the others. For that reason, a useful analysis compares examples rather than treating the first explanation as final.

When evidence is limited, the most responsible conclusion is often conditional. A statement may be true under one set of circumstances but unreliable under another. Recognizing that difference prevents a simple observation from becoming an exaggerated rule.

The passage therefore emphasizes a habit of thought: examine the conditions behind an outcome, test alternative explanations, and remain willing to revise the conclusion when new evidence appears.

The title, then, points to a question of method rather than a single answer. The most reliable approach is to distinguish observation from interpretation and to state the limits of the evidence alongside the conclusion.

title: The Language of Instructions
passage:
People encounter this issue in everyday life, yet common experience can make its causes difficult to notice. A familiar outcome may have several contributing factors, and changing one factor can alter the balance among the others. For that reason, a useful analysis compares examples rather than treating the first explanation as final.

When evidence is limited, the most responsible conclusion is often conditional. A statement may be true under one set of circumstances but unreliable under another. Recognizing that difference prevents a simple observation from becoming an exaggerated rule.

The passage therefore emphasizes a habit of thought: examine the conditions behind an outcome, test alternative explanations, and remain willing to revise the conclusion when new evidence appears.

The title, then, points to a question of method rather than a single answer. The most reliable approach is to distinguish observation from interpretation and to state the limits of the evidence alongside the conclusion.
